new_statements.rule_in_words: Ayu is described as a tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) plus rising and falling contours; the source contains no statement about word stress or accent at all, so no stress placement rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Tone is also used morphologically (tone-change is one of the noun-plural strategies, section 3.1; prefix tones 'driven by the stem-tone(s)', section 3.2).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms from a one-shot wordlist elicited from a single speaker (Shittu B. Salihu, Ungwar Nungu, Feb 2001 / Dec 2002); the author calls the transcription 'very preliminary'. Rising tone is printed with a corrupt diacritic in the PDF text layer (wɔ&k); rendered here as wɔ̌k per the table label 'Rising'.
new_statements.identity_note: Blench's data are from Ungwar Nungu village (5 km north of Fadan Ayu, Kaduna State), a single speaker; no dialect division is named, so the material is taken as the language-level variety ayuu1242 (alt. name Aya). Classification within Plateau is unsettled (Ninzic? per Blench; South-Central Plateau suggested in the draft).

new_statements.relation_note: This is the same document as the existing statement's source (the 2011-10-19 printout). The open_url is a the Internet Archive wildcard listing; web.archive.org was could not be reached by automated download at (automated download rc=7 'Couldn't connect', plain and with --resolve 207.241.237.3, two attempts). The on-disk copy was read instead; Confirms the catalog's tone-language / no-stress-statement reading; nothing to add on stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ayu is a register-tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) plus rising and falling contours; tone is lexically contrastive (minimal-ish pairs given) and also does morphological work (tone-change is one of the plural strategies, section 3.1). The manuscript says nothing about word stress or accent: a full-text search for stress/accent/prominen over all 24 pages returns 0 hits, and the phonology section (2.1 vowels, 2.2 consonants, 2.3 tones) has no suprasegmental heading other than tones.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the rising-tone example prints as 'wɔ&k' in the text layer (legacy SILDoulosIPA glyph for the wedge), read as wɔ̌k
new_statements.identity_note: Blench's data were collected with Barau Kato from Shittu B. Salihu of Ungwar Nungu (Fadan Ayu area), Kaduna State, Nigeria, which matches Glottolog ayuu1242 (9.26N 8.60E). Gerhardt's title localises the language as 'Südwest-Plateau, Nigeria' (same Ayu; not opened). No dialect split is described in either.
